request.statement:
Old decks never trusted a clerk to erase a temporary merely because its punch looked idle. Your job is to audit one such control deck.

Define `audit_deck(var_count, cards, normal_edges, exception_edges, entry)`.

Variables are numbered `0..var_count-1`; cards are numbered `0..len(cards)-1`. Each card is a four-item sequence:

`(targets, reads, effect, may_throw)`

- `targets` lists the variables written simultaneously by the card. An empty list denotes an observation card.
- `reads` lists variables read before any write by that card.
- `effect` is a Boolean indicating an externally visible side effect.
- `may_throw` is a Boolean.

A card with targets is one indivisible parallel assignment: after all reads, successful completion writes every listed target atomically. Duplicate entries in either list have no additional meaning.

Each edge list contains `(source, destination)` pairs. Normal edges are possible after successful completion. Exception edges are possible after the card's reads but before any of its writes, and therefore may originate only at cards with `may_throw == True`. A card may have any number of either kind of successor.

First mark cards reachable from `entry`, following every normal edge and every exception edge whose source may throw. Unreachable cards never participate further.

Among reachable cards, repeatedly perform erasure rounds. A parallel-assignment card is erasable in a round exactly when:

1. it has no side effect;
2. it cannot throw; and
3. for every variable it targets, after that card completes normally there is no possible control-flow path on which that variable is read before another successfully completed card writes it.

The entire card is erased or retained; individual targets cannot be erased separately. Reads occur before writes. If a later parallel assignment throws, none of its writes complete, so every older value remains available along that exception path. Previously erased cards are blank cards: they perform no reads or writes, cannot throw, and retain their normal edges. Observation cards are never erasable.

Erase all cards qualifying in a round simultaneously, then test again. Stop when a complete round erases nothing.

Return one string with one character per card, in card-number order:

- `U` for initially unreachable;
- `D` for reachable parallel assignments eventually erased;
- `K` for every reachable card retained.

All inputs are valid. `1 <= len(cards) <= 3000`, `1 <= var_count <= 1000`, there are at most 12000 edges total and at most 20000 listed reads plus targets. Lists may contain duplicates. Use only the Python standard library; perform no input/output and use no global mutable state.
